coverage_note: Many Medi turns are Latin-transliterated by the engine (02:44-05:57, 12:55-17:16, 32:21-36:09, 1:02:19-1:04:23), so forms there are low-confidence. 36:49-42:51 Medi's Arabic is lost as '[يتحدث العربية]' (the قلق/حرب/بعزم stretch, incl. 39:18 بأى -> بألقى which Amal called No: a dropped root letter, S4 pronunciation, not filed). 12:04 عروسك/عريس is Amal's joke on her own 'your bride' prompt, not filed. 29:59 ما بعتلهم: Amal conceded his masculine 'you' was fine. Engine: 18:27 شي قريب = شي غريب, 18:34 'صار my مبارة' = صار معي مبارح, 1:03:22 kana = kamaan likely. No echo-candidates file for 10-27. Proper names (Mahdi, برن) not glossed. medi_turns = 232 Arabic-script Medi lines + ~58 Latin-Arabic ones.

rows.medi_said: Asif la şugul ili ana atin-- ati-atik.

rows.english: sorry for the work that I gave you

rows.medi_said: lyom shribet ahwe ma crema wu maye keteer,
rows.why: English/Italian 'crema' inside an Arabic sentence; sheet row: 'cream | Kraima | كريمة | kraima'. Pre-ruled AR-1933 (ok to switch).

rows.why: فامي is not the Arabic word for dark; Amal supplied غامق, explained غميق is 'deep', and repeated 'غامق. Deep'; sheet: 'dark (color) | 8aameq | غامق'.
Noun after hada keeps el- (hada el-ishi); she praised the preposition use and let this pass; engine text is fragmentary (ماكس = Mahdi).

rows.medi_said: so I ask you would be أسألك.
rows.why: طلب takes من, not an object ending; Amal said No twice and he moved to منك (from you).

rows.medi_said: أسألك، uh، هدية من عروس، uh، عروسك.

rows.why: For 'wait for me' he put -ki (you) on the verb; Amal said in English what his form meant ('That I wait for you') and he fixed it to estenani.

rows.amal_said: شوفني. شوفني is see me. Look at me.
rows.why: Asked for 'look at me' he said شوفني; Amal pointed out شوفني is 'see me' and repeated 'Look at me', and he moved to itala (اطلع); she first said mm-hmm, so low.
اطلع takes على, not an object ending; Amal said 'Preposition.' and he fixed it to itala alay; sheet: 'i look at | bat6alla3 3ala'.
'Why is he looking at you' needs the he-form bit6alla3; he used the I-form batala; Amal prompted 'He is.' and he fixed to bitala alayk.
rows.english: why is he looking at you

rows.medi_said: Uh, answer to the-- Is it la?
rows.why: He asked which preposition جاوب takes, guessing la; Amal supplied على and said the preposition is optional, so a didn't-know, not a slip.
'Did they call you' needs the past rannu; he used a non-past form; Amal repeated the English prompt and he said 'Oh, past tense... ranno alayki'.

rows.medi_said: A period of time. Oh, زمان.
rows.amal_said: No. زمان is like long time ago ... or long time. Long, long time. فترة.
rows.why: For 'a while / period of time' he gave زمان (long ago); Amal said No and supplied فترة.
rows.english: a while, a period of time

rows.medi_said: أنا صار لي أدرس عربي، لا فاتحة-- لا فاتحة.
rows.amal_said: And the verb after it doesn't, it doesn't have to lose the be. عادي. ... Yes.

rows.medi_said: صار له فترة، uh، صديق. And he's been my friend for a while.
rows.why: 'my friend' needs the -i ending; Amal said 'My friend.' and he fixed to صديقي.

rows.why: He said a distorted فترة (engine wrote فاتحة here and at 21:06); Amal supplied فترة and he repeated it; may be mid-sentence help or the engine mishearing, so low.

rows.amal_said: Does مستـ، does بستنى take a preposition؟ ... نستناه لفترة.
rows.why: استنى takes no preposition, the person rides on the verb; Amal asked if it takes one, he said 'it doesn't. So just نستنى', she gave نستناه لفترة.
rows.english: let's wait for him for a while

rows.amal_said: you said نستنى شوي. شوي is not. Either شوي or فترة. ... No، لفترة.
rows.why: 'for a while' is la- + فترة; he stacked شوية فترة; Amal: 'Either شوي or فترة', 'No، لفترة' and repeated لفترة.
بعت takes la- for the person (ابعتلي); he put -ni on the verb; Amal asked what ببعت takes, he said بعتلي and she recast the command ابعتيلي.

rows.medi_said: nekhatat la o- nekhatat la oros.
rows.why: He meant their own wedding but said 'a wedding' (no el- / no -na); Amal said 'A wedding.' and he fixed to erosna, then she confirmed لا العرس.

rows.why: For 'meet me' he used etla3 (look / go out); Amal said لا and supplied التقي twice, he said 'You're right, iltei'; sheet: 'i meet | Ana balte2i'.

rows.right: ilteiti bi il zibayan / mai il zibayan

rows.why: خوّف is 'to scare someone', خاف is 'to be scared'; Amal said No and he fixed to تخاف; sheet: 'i worry about / fear for | bakhaaf 3ala'.

rows.medi_said: So هو، هو-- Is it أأل؟ أألأ؟
rows.why: Past of قلق for he is 2ele2 (sheet: 'he worried | huwwe 2ele2'); he tried أأل / أألأ, Amal prompted 'Internal flip' and gave إله.
'I told him' needs the past I-form 2ult; he tried أله / ألهت, Amal gave قلت and he built قلت له.
'He told you' needs the he-form قال; he used قلت (I told); Amal said 'He told.' and gave قالك, he said قال.
'They told me' needs the they-form 2aloo-li; engine wrote أله لي (he told me); she said Nice, so possibly the engine dropped -u.
'He told them' is قالهم; his قلهم is the command 'tell them'; Amal recast قالهم and asked what قلهم means, he said 'command tense'.
Paying with a card takes bi, not ma3 (engine ما = ma3); Amal said No and he said بي.
Prompt was the command 'Push the door'; he used the he-form يدفع (el- self-fixed); she said Mm-hmm.
'Pay us' needs the command ادفع and لنا (us); he said يدفع لي (he pays me); Amal recast ادفع لنا and he repeated يدفع لنا.
Talking to Amal (f) he said masculine بتقدر but then feminine تدفعي; she let it pass.
